projects.title: UK Retail GenAI Analytics Copilot
projects.business_question: Can a retail manager ask plain-English questions and receive reconciled numerical answers and evidence-backed explanations?

data.mode: Actual historical UK retailer transactions, December 2009–December 2011; NOT real-time
data.status: Full archive retrieved 30 October 2026; 1,067,371 rows ingested and audited. See project evidence/source_manifest.json and profile.json. Historical observations remain 2009–2011.

data.mode: Regularly published monthly GB macro context, separately labelled; not current merchant transactions
data.status: Verify download/API at build time; do not join unrelated periods or businesses

deliverables: Full-source ingestion, deduplication audit and reproducible DuckDB/Parquet warehouse
LangGraph bounded tool workflow: validated read-only SQL for numbers, RAG for schema/product/source context, local LLM explanations
Runnable API/UI showing query evidence, source dates and abstention
Held-out task evaluation against deterministic SQL/lexical baselines, with accuracy, grounding, failure and latency results
CI, replay fixtures, source register, model licence/version, monitoring and beginner/interview case study
n8n workflow export for manual/scheduled ingestion or freshness checks calling the local API, with idempotence, retries and run evidence
acceptance: Target full 1,067,371 source rows; report actual raw/clean counts and exclusions, missing customers and cancellation handling
Do not describe transaction rows as vector documents; report actual distinct indexed descriptions/docs/chunks
No unrestricted SQL writes or arbitrary agent execution; bound query cost, tool calls and input size
At least 40 held-out numerical/retrieval/unsupported tasks with saved references; keep tuning tasks separate and label AI-authored evaluation
Actually run free local LLM inference and show generated outputs; if unavailable, mark GenAI requirement blocked rather than substituting templates as an LLM
Reconcile numeric answers to independent SQL controls; do not invent costs, profit, stock, ROI or live sales

projects.title: UK Retail Demand ML and MLOps Service
projects.business_question: Can a reproducible model forecast next-week product demand more accurately than simple baselines, and can its predictions be served and monitored?
tools: Hugging Face model/dataset tooling where applicable

data.mode: Historical UK transactions; distinct predictive objective from W01, not live inventory or sales
data.status: Reuse verified ingestion only after auditing W01 outputs; report aggregate series counts separately from raw rows

deliverables: As-of product-week demand target, causal lag features and rolling temporal backtests
Actually fitted ML model and small CPU neural comparator, training-only preprocessing and simple last-week/seasonal baselines
Saved predictions, per-product and aggregate MAE/WAPE with zero-demand handling and negative results
Versioned local experiment/artifact tracking, batch inference and validated prediction API
Data/feature drift replay, quality gates, CI, model card, monitoring/runbook and interview explanation
acceptance: Fix target, forecast horizon, returns treatment and product eligibility before testing; no future-derived filtering or random row split
Separate train/validation/test chronologically, group overlapping forecast windows appropriately and freeze test selection
Report actual training rows/time/epochs/parameters, machine resources, package/model versions and baseline comparisons
Fit a small neural model rather than a placeholder; do not claim neural methods win if simpler models do better
Evaluate unavailable/new products explicitly; no claim of inventory optimisation, causal impact, current retail demand or profit
Distinct code/service/evaluation from W01 copilot; shared source ingestion does not make it a second copy of that project

Deep learning is required: train a small CPU PyTorch MLP/LSTM/TCN as appropriate, save weights/configuration and learning curves, report epochs, parameters, training time and held-out comparison with simple and non-neural ML baselines; no foundation-model training claim
